To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microtubule associated proteins are expressed in a cell type and developmental stage specific manner, and that their mRNA is localized to the cell body, dendrites and axons of developing and adult brain neurons.
microtubule associated proteins, MAP1, MAP5, and MAP2, have distinct patterns of expression during development of rat brain.
the microtubule associated proteins (MAPs) are differentially localized in neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of microtubules in neuronal development, and the molecular and cellular basis for microtubule heterogeneity in neuronal processes.
the mechanisms of neuronal development, and in particular with the role of microtubules and microtubule associated proteins (MAPs) in this process.
the regulation of gene expression in the developing and regenerating brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microtubule associated protein genes are expressed in a highly regulated manner during brain development.

MAP1, MAP5, and beta-tubulin are all transported from their site of synthesis, the neuronal cell body, to the distal processes, while the MAP2 mRNA is localized within the cell body and is not transported.
the MAPs are not only involved in the assembly and maintenance of microtubules, but also in their function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MAPs are not just structural proteins but play a major role in regulating neuronal development and differentiation.
the microtubules in the dendrites and the cell bodies of mature neurons contain MAP1, while the microtubule in the axon contain MAP1, 2, and 5.
the microtubules of neurons are heterogeneous in composition, function, and localization and that these properties are regulated at the level of the gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAPs are differentially compartmentalized within neurons.
the distribution of MAP mRNA within neurons changes during development, and that the distribution of the protein is not the same as the mRNA.
microtubule associated protein (MAP) mRNA is localized to specific regions of the cell in both the developing and adult brain, and that this localization is regulated.
